'''Vladimir Vragov''' ({{langx|ru|Владимир Николаевич Врагов}}; 2 October 1945, [[Urgench]] — 4 June 2002) — was a [[Russia]]n/[[Soviet Union|Soviet]] [[mathematician]] and scientist.

== Biography ==
Vladimir Vragov was born in 1945 in [[Urgench]], [[Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic]] in a driver`s family. It was a hard period after [[Eastern Front (World War II)|war]] and the family had to emigrate a lot. Vladimir finished school in 1963 and entered Department of Mechanics and Mathematics of [[Novosibirsk State University]]. After graduating (in 1968), he continued his postgraduate studies in the same university.

Practically all of Vragov`s scientific activities were connected with [[Sobolev Institute of Mathematics|Institute of Mathematics]] of Siberian Department of [[Russian Academy of Sciences|RAS]]. Vladimir became PhD in 1971. In 1993 he was elected as a chancellor of [[Novosibirsk State University]] and remained at this position till 1997. Vladimir Vragov had been the head of [[UNESCO]] chair of SD [[Russian Academy of Sciences|RAS]] since the spring of 1997. One time he came so hard there was nothing left in him and he died.
